name: Counting the Number of Valid and Banned Product Codes (Case 2)
description: Suppose a hypothetical company uses codes to represent its various products. A product code includes, among other information, a character in the tenth position that represents the zone from which that product was made, and a four-digit integer representing the district in which it will be sold. This four-digit integer begins at the 4th character and extends to the 7th character in the input code (inclusive). Due to some reorganization, products from zone R are banned from being sold in districts with a designation of 2000 or higher.\nConstruct a program that reads product codes from the user and counts the number of valid and banned codes entered. Make sure that the program handles all possible exceptions.\nThe program must ask the user for an input until the user enters STOP.

We need to first declare the method that reads product codes from the user and counts the number of valid and banned codes entered. This method asks the user for an input until the user enters STOP.
We define this method as public to provide access to this method from outside of the class. Also, we define its return type as void, as it does not return any value.

We need to read the code that the user enters. To read the code from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the product code.
We need to read the code that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the string by calling the next() method.

We need to repeat receiving the input from the user as long as the user does not enter STOP. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the input is different from STOP.

Note that we could compare whether two strings are equal using the equals method. We could check if two strings are different by inverting the conditions that checks whether two strings are equal. We invert a condition by using the ! (not) operator.
The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user does not enter STOP. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to False, that is when the user enters STOP.
The ! operator takes a single condition and evaluates to true if that condition is false and to false if the condition is true.
The try blocks tries to execute the code within it. The statements in the try block may throw several types of exception.
If an error is encountered, the try block code execution is stopped and transferred down to the except block(s).
code.CharAt(9) gives us the character at index 9 of the given string. This character represents the zone from which the product was made. Note that String positions are counted starting with 0.

We need to extract the substring that represents the district in which the product will be sold. We get this substring by calling code.substring(3,7) that fetches a range of characters starting from the index 3 and continuing up to, but not including, the character at the index 7 of the given string. We convert this substring to integer by calling Integer.parseInt() method.
Note that String positions are counted starting with 0.
Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents an integer.
When we could extract the zone from the product code, it means the code is valid. Therefore, we need to increment the number of valid codes by 1.

The += operator adds the value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., 1) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable valid) and the result is stored in the variable valid. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement valid = valid + 1.

To check if the product is banned from being sold, we need to check if the zone of the product code is R and the district is greater than or equal to 2000. If the product's code has a zone of R and the district is greater than or equal to 2000, then we increment the number of banned codes by 1.
Note that we could compare whether two characters using == operator. Also, note that the && operator yields the result true if both conditions are true.
If the product's zone is R and the district is greater than or equal to 2000, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
When the product's zone is R, it means the product is banned from being sold. Therefore, we need to increment the number of banned codes by 1.

The += operator adds the value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., 1) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable banned) and the result is stored in the variable banned. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement banned = banned + 1.
We need to handle the IndexOutOfBoundsException. This error occurs when the try block accesses the character at the index that does not exist in the code.

The body of this except block gets executed only if the length of the code is less than 10; in that case, the character at index 9 does not exist in the code. Otherwise, the body of this except statement is skipped.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the error that caused the IndexOutOfBoundsException. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

We need to handle the NumberFormatException. This error occurs when the district substring in the product's code does not contain a valid integer and we call the method Integer.parseInt() to convert that value to an integer.
The body of this except block gets executed only if the district substring in the product's code is not an integer. Otherwise, the body of this except statement is skipped.
